original_question: Is it consistent that the additivity of the null ideal is strictly smaller than the additivity number add(S_1(O, O))?
target_in_paper: Section 8.3, Problem 12 ([3, Problem 4]): "Is it consistent that add(N) < add(S_1(O, O))?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact comparison asked in the paper: it is a consistency question about whether the additivity of the null ideal can be strictly smaller than add(S_1(O,O)). It also keeps the inequality in the correct direction and uses the same two cardinal characteristics that appear in the paper’s official formulation.
missing_details: The paper’s default setting is that spaces X are sets of reals (equivalently, homeomorphic to separable zero-dimensional metrizable spaces), unless stated otherwise.
S_1(O,O) should be spelled out: for every sequence (U_n : n in N) of open covers of X, one can choose a single element U_n from each cover so that {U_n : n in N} still covers X.
Figure 1 identifies S_1(O,O) with the Rothberger property, so naming that property makes the question more readable and paper-faithful.
To make add(S_1(O,O)) stand alone, one should define it as the least cardinal κ such that some union of κ many sets of reals, each satisfying S_1(O,O), fails to satisfy S_1(O,O).
The symbol N should be unpacked as the ideal of Lebesgue null subsets of R, so add(N) means the additivity of the null ideal.
The background theory for the word "consistent" should be made explicit as consistency with ZFC.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that add(N) < add(S_1(O,O)), where N is the ideal of Lebesgue null subsets of R, a set of reals X satisfies S_1(O,O) (the Rothberger property) if for every sequence of open covers (U_n : n in N) of X there exist U_n in U_n such that {U_n : n in N} is still an open cover of X, and add(S_1(O,O)) is the least cardinal κ for which there exists a family of κ sets of reals, each with property S_1(O,O), whose union does not satisfy S_1(O,O)?
justification: The draft is essentially Problem 12 verbatim. The only substantial omissions are the paper’s default ambient class of spaces (sets of reals), the definition of the selection principle S_1(O,O), the identification of S_1(O,O) with the Rothberger property, and the meaning of the additivity number add(S_1(O,O)). Section 8.3 explicitly places the question in the additivity-number program and states the exact inequality being asked about, after noting that add(N) <= add(S_1(O,O)) is already known.
